title: Gabi ng Aswang
cultural_note: The aswang is one of the best-known creatures in Philippine folklore, often said to look like an ordinary neighbor by day. Salt, garlic and oil of coconut are traditional protections.
short_description: Survive one night in a haunted barrio as the aswang hunts.
description: A fictional placeholder game. Lock your doors, ration your salt and garlic, and outlast a long night in a remote provincial barrio while something wicked stalks the rooftops.

title: Tikbalang Trail
cultural_note: The tikbalang is a tall, horse-headed creature said to lead travelers astray in forests. Folk belief says you can escape by wearing your shirt inside out.
short_description: Get lost on purpose, and outwit the trickster of the forest path.
description: A fictional placeholder game. Travel a mountain trail, trade riddles with the tikbalang, and learn the old tricks for finding your way home.

title: Diwata ng Bundok
cultural_note: Diwata are nature spirits in pre-colonial Philippine belief, often tied to a specific mountain, tree or river. Offerings were left to ask permission before gathering from their lands.
short_description: Restore a sleeping mountain with calm, cozy puzzles.
description: A fictional placeholder game. Tend the forest, solve gentle nature puzzles, and earn the trust of the diwata who watches over the mountain.

title: Tumbang Preso Turbo
cultural_note: Tumbang preso is a street game where players throw slippers to knock a can off its spot while the taya guards it. It is played in neighborhoods all over the country.
short_description: The classic street game, now with power-ups and chaos.
description: A fictional placeholder game. Knock the can, dodge the taya, and race your friends in fast-paced local multiplayer rounds set in a sunny neighborhood.

title: Maiba-Taya Royale
cultural_note: Maiba-taya is a tag game where the player who is 'it' (the taya) must tag others, and a player is safe by changing places. It teaches quick thinking and teamwork.
short_description: A tactical twist on tag: plan your swaps, trap the taya.
description: A fictional placeholder game. Turn-based tag on a tiny barangay map. Outmaneuver rival teams and keep your squad safe from the taya.

title: Katipunan Whispers
cultural_note: The Katipunan was a secret society founded in 1892 to win independence from Spain. Members used codes, aliases and blood compacts to keep their plans hidden.
short_description: Carry secret messages across 1890s Manila without being caught.
description: A fictional placeholder game. Play a young courier in a story-driven RPG about codes, loyalty and the quiet courage that came before the revolution.

title: Galyon ng Maynila
cultural_note: From 1565 to 1815 the Manila galleons carried silver from the Americas to Asia and silk and porcelain back. The trade made Manila a key link in early global commerce.
short_description: Run a galleon trade route between Manila and Acapulco.
description: A fictional placeholder game. Manage crews, cargo and storms across the Pacific in a deep trade-strategy game set in the age of the Manila galleons.

title: Jeepney Diaries
cultural_note: Jeepneys, originally built from leftover US military jeeps, are the most iconic public transport in the Philippines. Their bright paint and slogans make each one unique.
short_description: Drive a route, meet your pasahero, and decorate your own jeepney.
description: A fictional placeholder game. Pass the fare along ('bayad po!'), chat with passengers, and customize your jeepney as you grow your route.

title: Sari-Sari Simulator
cultural_note: The sari-sari store is a small neighborhood shop selling a bit of everything, often run from the front of a family home. Many sell goods in tingi (single pieces) and on utang (credit).
short_description: Stock the shelves and keep the neighborhood happy.
description: A fictional placeholder game. Run a corner store, sell candy by the piece, track utang, and handle rush hour after school.

title: Padala
cultural_note: Millions of Filipinos work overseas (OFWs) and send a padala, a package or remittance, to their families back home. Balikbayan boxes are a well-known symbol of this.
short_description: Pack a balikbayan box and keep a family close from far away.
description: A fictional placeholder game. Choose what to send home, read the replies, and follow one family across a year of distance and small joys.

title: Fiesta Fever
short_description: A rhythm party game packed with street-dance energy.
description: A fictional placeholder game. Tap to the beat through parades, games and feasts in a colorful town fiesta.

title: Starlight Drift
short_description: Explore a drifting archipelago of floating islands.
description: A fictional placeholder game. Sail between sky islands, recruit a crew, and uncover why the stars have started to fall.
